title: HTML markup review
when: The user wants HTML pages checked for valid structure, semantics, metadata and accessible markup before shipping.
prompt:
Goal: A markup review confirming document basics, semantic structure and accessible names, each defect with its element and fix.
Steps:
1. Basics per page: <!doctype html>, html lang, meta charset first, viewport meta, a unique title and meta description.
2. Structure: one h1, no skipped heading levels, header, nav, main and footer landmarks, lists for groups of links.
3. Semantics: button for actions, a for navigation, no clickable div or span, tables only for tabular data with th and scope.
4. Names: alt on every img (empty for decoration), a label per input, aria-label on icon buttons, link text that makes sense alone.
5. Hygiene: unique ids, no onclick= or style= attributes, scripts deferred or modules, rel="noopener" on target="_blank".
6. Nesting: every tag closed, no block inside inline elements, no interactive element inside another (a link inside a button).
Quality bar:
- Findings name the tag and where it is (file and nearby text).
- ARIA proposed only where native HTML cannot do it.
- Severity per finding.
Pitfalls:
- Adding roles that repeat native semantics (role="button" on button).
- Skipping metadata on secondary pages.
- Treating warnings as blockers.
Verify:
- [ ] Each page checked for doctype, lang, title and viewport.
- [ ] Heading outline written per page.
- [ ] All images and controls named.
- [ ] Nesting errors listed.
Output: review.md with a per page checklist result and the findings with fixes.

examples.input: check the HTML of my 4 page site
examples.output: about.html: two h1, missing meta description; contact.html: input without label; index.html ok
